title: SourceFlow workflow (sourceflow.workflow: 1)
description: The workflow DSL of SourceFlow Studio (design doc 15 §5). Structure only: references to message types, owners, routes and schemas are checked by the validator (WF-V01..V16). Workflow files are YAML without anchors or aliases.

name.description: The workflow name; with the version it is the process name name@version.

version.description: Structural changes to a published workflow need a new version (WF-V15).

owner.description: The orchestrating service; the workflow is generated into it.

description.description: What the workflow is for, in a sentence. Shown in Studio; it does not change the fingerprint.

start.description: The event that starts an instance, and how later messages find it.

data.description: Instance data. Captured fields are added from their event.

steps.description: The steps, run in order unless a step says next or a failure says goto.

on.description: What happens when an instance ends: completed, compensated, or stopped for an operator.

kebab.description: Lower-case words of letters and digits joined by hyphens, for example order-fulfilment.

identifier.description: A field name: letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit.

messageType.description: A message type as {name}.v{version}, for example payments.charge.v1.

duration.description: An ISO-8601 duration without years and months: PT30S, PT5M, PT1H, P1D, P1DT12H.

guard.description: A CESQL boolean expression over $data.*, event.data.* (doc 15 §5.2).

on.description: The start event: a domain event of the owner, or an integration event the owner subscribes to.

correlate.description: The path in the start event of the instance id, for example data.orderId. Awaited events that carry the same field correlate by it (WF-V04).

when.description: Starts an instance only when this guard over event.data.* holds.

start.description: The event that starts an instance, and how later messages find it.

from.description: Copies the value from the start event, for example start.data.total.

type.description: The field type when it is not copied from the start event.

default.description: The initial value of a typed field.

personal.description: Personal data: crypto-shredded in the workflow state (WF-V14).

dataField.description: One field of the instance data: copied from the start event (from), or typed with an optional default.

id.description: The step id: lower-case words joined by hyphens, unique in the workflow; complete is reserved.

send.description: The command the step sends to its owner. Without it, the step only waits.

await.description: What the step waits for: the success event, and the failures it handles.

timeout.description: How long the step waits, and what happens then. Every wait needs one, or none with a reason (WF-V06).

compensate.description: How to undo the step after a later failure: compensations run in reverse order (WF-V09).

pivot.description: The point of no return: later failures recover forward (WF-V07).

when.description: A guard over $data.*: when it doesn't hold, the step is skipped.

next.description: The step after a success, or complete.

step.description: A step: send a command (or nothing), wait for its outcome, and say what happens on failure, on timeout and when undoing.

command.description: The command, owned by exactly one service (WF-V02).

map.description: The command's fields, each a $data path, an event.data path (start event, first step), $failure.code, a literal, or a $hook (WF-V12).

send.description: A command and the values of its fields.

oneOf.description: A path: $data.<field>, event.data.<field> (the start event, in the first step only) or $failure.code / $failure.message (in on.compensated).
A literal number, boolean or null (null only into a nullable field).
A value computed in C#: a static partial method of that name on the generated workflow record (SF0021 when it is missing).

success.description: The event that completes the step (WF-V03).

failure.description: The rejections and failure events the step handles; anything else stops the instance for an operator.

await.description: The success event and the failures a step handles.

capture.description: Instance data to take from the event, for example paymentId: event.data.paymentId.

when.description: The event completes the step only when this guard over $data.* and event.data.* holds.

success.description: The success event, as a message type, or with captures and a guard.

rejected.description: A rejection code of the command (WF-V08: in its rejects, with replyOnReject on a remote route).

retry.description: Sends the command again before giving up (business retry).

then.description: What happens when the retries are used up.

failure.description: One failure a step handles: a rejection of its command, or a failure event.

oneOf.description: No timeout; WF-V06 asks for the object form with a reason.

none.description: No timeout (the step can wait for ever); give the reason.

reason.description: Why the wait has no timeout.

retry.description: Sends the command again when an attempt times out.

then.description: What happens when the last attempt times out (default fail).

timeout.description: A wait's timeout: after a duration, retried, then what happens; or none with a reason.

retry.description: Bounded re-attempts; WF-V10 checks 1 <= max <= 20 and the delays.

backoff.description: The delay between attempts: always initial (fixed), or doubling from initial (exponential). Without initial, attempts follow at once.

oneOf.description: fail compensates the completed steps (only before the pivot, WF-V07); manual stops the instance for an operator; complete ends it as completed.

then.description: fail (compensate, only before the pivot), manual (stop for an operator), complete, or { goto: step }.

oneOf.description: WF-V09 asks for the object form with a reason.

success.description: The event that confirms the undo.

await.description: The event that confirms the undo.

retry.description: Sends the undoing command again after a rejection or a timeout; when it gives up, the instance stops for an operator.

timeout.description: How long each undo attempt waits.

none.description: The step has nothing to undo; give the reason.

reason.description: Why the step needs no compensation.

compensate.description: How to undo a step: a command and the event that confirms it, with a retry and a timeout; or none with a reason.

compensated.description: Sent when the instance was compensated; $failure.code and $failure.message say why.

alert.description: Counts the instance on the alert metric.

manual.description: An instance stopped for an operator: alert: true counts it on the sourceflow.workflow.manual_intervention metric.

on.description: What happens when an instance ends.
